title: Fixed-point tensor network for compactified boson conformal field theory
authors: Gong Cheng, Dong-Yu Bao, Zheng-Cheng Gu
abstract: Fixed-point (FP) tensor networks provide a discrete spacetime representation of conformal field theories (CFTs), offering a new route toward understanding holographic duality, generalized symmetries, and even quantum gravity. In this work, we construct FP tensors for the 2D compactified boson theory at a generic compactification radius, an archetypal irrational CFT, using boundary (open-string) data with conformal boundary conditions. We show that the resulting tensors reproduce the closed-string spectrum with high accuracy and generate stable renormalization-group (RG) flows under the tensor complex renormalization algorithm. Moreover, we identify a controllable exactly marginal deformation at the level of a single tensor, enabling flows that move continuously along the $c=1$ moduli space. This framework establishes a concrete lattice-level route toward describing a broad class of 2D irrational CFTs.
summary: This paper develops a powerful fixed-point tensor network framework to discretize and analyze irrational Conformal Field Theories, specifically the compactified boson CFT. By constructing tensors from boundary correlation functions and applying renormalization group techniques, the authors accurately reproduce continuum spectra and demonstrate control over marginal deformations. This provides a concrete lattice approach for studying complex quantum field theories.
main_problem: The work aims to extend fixed-point (FP) tensor network constructions for Conformal Field Theories (CFTs) from tractable rational settings to the more complex irrational regime.
main_result: The authors successfully construct and verify FP tensors for the 2D compactified boson CFT, demonstrating a lattice-level description that accurately reproduces the closed-string spectrum and allows for continuous marginal deformations along the c=1 moduli space.
method: They employ tensor network contractions (rank-3 and rank-4) within the Tensor Complex Renormalization (TCR) algorithm to map continuum CFT physics onto a discrete lattice representation.
model_or_system: The system studied is the 2D compactified boson theory, an archetypal irrational CFT relevant in string theory and condensed matter physics (like Luttinger liquids). The construction uses boundary data derived from Dirichlet and Neumann boundary conditions.
key_observables: Closed-string spectrum ($\Delta$), central charge ($c$), and scaling dimensions ($\Delta$) extracted via transfer matrix diagonalization and TCR analysis.
important_parameters: Compactification radius ($R$), finite grid sizes ($\Lambda_D, \Lambda_N$), and the deformation parameter $	au$ controlling marginal flow.
main_assumptions: The continuous nature of parameters is handled by discretizing them onto finite grids; convergence to the continuum limit requires retaining an increasing number of descendant states.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the RG spectrum obtained from both rank-3 and refined rank-4 FP tensors at specific radii, showing systematic recovery of the expected conformal dimensions. One figure also tracks how varying a geometric parameter ($	au$) induces continuous flow along the moduli space.
paper_structure: The paper builds by first establishing the tensor structure using boundary correlation functions (rank-3/4). It then applies the TCR algorithm to verify stability and calculate spectra for specific radii, culminating in demonstrating controlled marginal deformations by modifying the geometry of the tensors.
why_interesting: While focused on CFTs, the core methodology—using tensor networks (TCR) to simulate continuum physics and study RG flows—is highly relevant to numerical methods used in AMO physics for simulating quantum many-body systems or open quantum dynamics.
